subject: IQCore inference characterization: proposed test plan and clarifications

From: Michael Trent <mtrent@iqcore.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@iqcore.com>

Subject: IQCore RFI: Performance characterization questions

Sofia,

Thanks for engaging on the RFI. Attached is the performance tab from our RFI workbook (RFI_Performance_Questions_v2.xlsx) — we need concrete inputs for the benchmarking section so our infra / procurement teams can align on sizing and SLA language. High level asks:

- Typical throughput targets (QPS) and observed throughput under 95th/99th latency SLOs for text generation endpoints.
- Tail latency numbers (p50/p95/p99) with sequence length 128 and 1024 and with/without batching.
- Explanation of test methodology: synthetic load vs replay traffic, hardware used, warm/cold start definitions, caching strategy (prefix/KV cache), and how you handle stateful (chat) contexts.
- Any recommended load profiles and the test harness you expect customers to run for validation.
- Notes on behavior under saturation and graceful degradation (fallbacks to smaller variants, queueing, shedding).

Can you provide a written response and a short test plan we can share with our SRE/benchmarking team? Ideally by end of week so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Michael Trent
Senior Procurement Manager
IQCore Analytics

Michael — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the details and a reproducible test plan. High-level summary here, full workbook and harness README attached. If anything below doesn't map to your team's needs, flag specific rows in the spreadsheet and we'll adjust.

Summary of our approach (short):
- Metrics we report: throughput (QPS), latency (p50/p95/p99), time-to-first-token (TTFT), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and estimated $/1M tokens.
- Test environments: canonical runs on NVIDIA A100 80GB (hosted equivalent), instance-level runs on T4 and A10 for smaller SKUs. We also provide quantized 4-bit model variants and FP16 variants for comparative runs.
- Sequence lengths & scenarios: standard gen workloads at 128 tokens and long-form at 1,024 tokens. We run both single-prompt stateless generation and stateful chat with 5-10 message context to measure KV cache impact.
- Warm vs cold: cold = fresh process + empty model cache + no warmed KV cache; warm = persistent process with KV cache seeded by a 10k-token prefix sweep to simulate hot routing. We will report both.
- Batching: tests include single-request (batch=1), micro-batch (batch sizes 2/4/8 with dynamic batching enabled), and large batch (up to 64) for throughput peak measurement. We document batching latencies and per-request tail effects.
- Load styles: replay of customer traces (if IQCore can provide anonymized traces) and synthetic Poisson/step/ramp profiles. For procurement, recommend a 30-min ramp-to-peak + 30-min soak + 15-min spike profile.
- Degradation behavior: we test queueing latency growth, configured shedding thresholds, and automatic fallback routes to smaller model variants. We'll include load-vs-error and load-vs-latency curves.

Proposed deliverables and timeline:
1) Written RFI response (spreadsheet populated) — attached — delivered same day.
2) Test harness README and Docker image reference (attached README, image: redwood/test-harness:20260825).
3) Two benchmark runs (A100 FP16 and 4-bit quant) on hosted test pool with results and raw logs — scheduled 48-72 hours after you sign off on the plan.
4) SRE call to walk through results and any reproduction on your side.

Questions for you:
- Can IQCore provide a representative request trace (anonymized) or should we rely on our synthetic profiles?
- Are there specific SLAs (p99 ≤ X ms at Y QPS) you want validated? If you share target numbers we can tailor runs.

Attached: iqcore-rfi-performance-spreadsheet.xlsx, redwood-test-harness-README.md

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications / notes we will include in the workbook and test scripts: 

- Warmup sweep: our recommended warmup script performs a randomized prefix sweep of ~10k tokens across the model to populate weight caches and JIT kernels; for KV cache warm state we replay 1-2 long contexts that match your expected chat lengths. This produces deterministic improvement in p95/p99 vs cold starts.

- Repro scripts: we will provide a docker-compose that runs the harness, a load injector (wrk-style plus a token-aware client), and a lightweight log collector (Fluentd -> S3). Command example: 
  docker run --rm redwood/test-harness:20260825 "--profile=iqcore-ramp30-soak30-spike15 --seq-len=128,1024 --batch=1,4,16"

- Measurement windows: 5-min steady-state snapshots plus aggregate over full run; p50/p95/p99 computed on server-observed response times including queueing. Token accounting is per-generated token.

- Autoscaling and queueing: when we test autoscaling policies we include cold-scale penalties (time to spin GPU pods) and a pre-warm policy that retains a minimum pool sized by your 95th-percentile concurrent requests. We'll publish the autoscaler config used.

- Fallbacks: we support policy-based fallback to a smaller variant (same architecture, lower precision) and can auto-swap to CPU-based safe-fallback with de-rated throughput. We will show step-down latency and token cost tradeoffs.

I also added a short example config to the README for trace sampling and how to attach x-trace ids into the harness so IQCore SREs can reconcile logs with your observability.

-Marcus
